description: I’m a Software Engineering student passionate about AI web development, and solving real-world problems through technology. For this challenge, I’m interested in building an interactive and practical Martian mapping solution that combines NASA datasets into a useful explorer’s guide. I’m looking for teammates with skills in astronomy or geospatial data, UI/UX, data analysis, storytelling, and creative problem-solving.
summary:
Sol Atlas is an interactive 3D Mars map that works as a survival guide for planning safe crewed walks, built entirely on real NASA mission data. You can fly from a globe of Mars, with Viking colour, MOLA topography, Mars Odyssey night-infrared and USGS geology layers, down into Jezero Crater and a 6 × 6 km Marswalk zone built from HiRISE and CTX imagery and elevation models.

Pick any point in the zone and Sol Atlas finds the lowest-oxygen route over the terrain. You can then simulate the walk in helmet view, with live oxygen, slope, speed and position. It also shows Perseverance’s real drive path and photos, the Mars clock and the Earth–Mars signal delay.

This answers the challenge by turning scattered NASA data into one map that astronauts and mission planners can actually use. It matters because oxygen, terrain and distance from help are the limits on any Mars walk, and Sol Atlas lets crews test a route before they take a step. The code is open source, and estimates are labelled in the app.
details:
WHAT IT DOES AND HOW IT WORKS

Sol Atlas is an interactive 3D Mars map that works as a survival guide for planning a crewed walk. It starts as a rotating globe with switchable NASA layers: Viking color, MOLA/HRSC topography, Mars Odyssey night-infrared and the USGS geologic map, plus NASA's Human Exploration Zones. From there you descend into Jezero Crater and into a 6 x 6 km Marswalk zone built from HiRISE and CTX imagery and elevation models. In the zone you pick any point on the map, and a route search finds the lowest-oxygen path over the real terrain, using a walking-speed and metabolic model driven by slope. You can then simulate the walk in helmet view, with live oxygen, slope, speed and position, and the skyline an astronaut would see. The app also shows Perseverance's real drive path and raw photos at each science stop, the Mars clock and sol, and the Earth-Mars signal delay.

BENEFITS AND INTENDED IMPACT

Oxygen, terrain and distance from help limit every Mars walk. Sol Atlas lets mission planners, students and the public test a route and see its cost before a step is taken, so crews can choose safer paths and plan reserves. Scattered NASA datasets become one map that anyone can read in a browser, on a laptop or a phone. We hope it shows how open NASA data can support planning for the first human missions.

TOOLS, LANGUAGES AND SOFTWARE

JavaScript with three.js for the 3D globe and terrain, GLSL shaders, HTML and CSS, built with Vite. Python (rasterio, NumPy, Pillow, SciPy) processes the NASA/USGS map files into web-ready data. Playwright was used for testing and Netlify for hosting. Fonts: Rajdhani, Orbitron and JetBrains Mono. AI tools: Claude Code and Claude (Anthropic). No special hardware was needed; we developed and tested on laptops and phones.

HOW IT IS CREATIVE

It treats Mars like a planning game map but uses only real mission data. You zoom from a whole planet to one footstep, see through an astronaut's helmet, and follow where the real rover actually drove. Estimates are labelled openly in the app, and a Data Sources window credits every layer.

FACTORS WE CONSIDERED

Honesty: anything approximate (weather and radiation values, our proposed landing zone, suit assumptions) is marked as an estimate and not shown as live data.

Accuracy: slope limits and the oxygen model come from published methods (Pandolf, Tobler).

Accessibility: it runs in a normal browser and works on phones. Openness: the code is open source (Apache 2.0) and every dataset and AI tool is credited.

Safety and privacy: no recognizable people under 18 appear in the project.
